plan.p0: Frame-portal hypothesis: Treat the non-background cells as an incomplete rectangular frame. Fill background gaps between frame cells with 8, and extend each such gap outward to the nearest grid edge in the perpendicular direction. Existing colored cells remain unchanged. This assumes only frame-boundary gaps emit rays.
plan.p1: Independent line hypothesis: In every row or column, fill background cells between two non-background cells with 8; a line containing a single marker may also extend from that marker toward the outside of the marker bounding box. This assumes each row/column acts independently rather than belonging to one frame.
plan.p2: Connected-object hypothesis: Group the non-background cells into one object, identify its extreme horizontal rows and vertical sides, and treat missing cells on those extremes as openings. Color openings and their outward continuations 8. This assumes object connectivity and extreme geometry matter, so detached markers could be ignored or handled separately.
plan.p3: Pattern-completion hypothesis: Regard the marker arrangement as a partial repeated/template motif; infer the missing aligned segments and copy them as 8 along matching rows or columns, preserving markers. This assumes continuation follows repeated spacing or symmetry, rather than always reaching the boundary.
